gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-entity acquisition of Federal-Mogul by Tenneco, with Federal-Mogul merged into Tenneco at closing. There is no evidence of a structural mismatch between products (T4) and processes (T5), or between processes (T5) and organization (T6) at closing, as the entire entity transferred.

grok.rationale: At closing Federal-Mogul was acquired via all membership interests and merged with and into Tenneco as surviving company, with no carve-out; the slice states no transition-services bridge was identified, so customer-facing product/brands (Motorparts and Powertrain) and the operational processes that produce them crossed together (gap_45=0). The same whole-entity merger brought Federal-Mogul’s organization into the combined company under Tenneco board and co-CEO designations drawn from incumbent Tenneco leadership, so processes and organization transferred in one step without a documented process-vs-people structural mismatch at closing (gap_56=0).

openai.rationale: The transaction acquired all Federal-Mogul membership interests and merged Federal-Mogul into Tenneco, so its Motorparts and Powertrain products moved with the whole operating business; no carve-out or transition-services bridge was identified, supporting gap_45 = 0. At closing, incumbent Tenneco executives were assigned to lead the combined Aftermarket & Ride Performance and Powertrain Technology businesses under Tenneco's board, documenting management alignment alongside the transferred operations rather than a process-organization mismatch, supporting gap_56 = 0.
